sources.entry: Web - Minimal AI browser for macOS, built with SwiftUI. [![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/nuance-dev/Web)

summary.one_liner: A native macOS web browser built with SwiftUI that includes local AI features running on the Mac via MLX.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a browser with a sidebar or top tab bar that can be shown, hidden, or moved, plus a command palette opened with ⌘K for finding tabs and commands. A "Glance" quick-lookup window is summoned with ⌃⌥Space and can be pinned or opened in a tab. Focus Mode (⇧⌘B) hides the chrome to show only the page. An assistant can ask about or summarize the current page, using a local MLX model, a provider API key, or a compatible self-hosted server. Pages can be bookmarked, searched, and private tabs are available; session restore can be turned on. The README states that page sharing with an API is off by default and that private pages are excluded.
use_cases: browse the web on a Mac with a minimal interface
ask questions about a web page with a local AI model
summarize the page I am reading
quick lookups in a floating window while working
keep browsing sessions and tabs across restarts
how_to_run: Run the Web scheme in Xcode (ad-hoc signing, no Apple Developer account needed)
For a stripped local build, run ./scripts/build-release.sh
notable: Local AI assistant that runs MLX models on the Mac, with optional cloud provider API keys or a self-hosted compatible server
Glance floating quick-lookup window on a global shortcut, pinnable or openable as a tab
Focus Mode hides the browser chrome to show only the page
Private pages are excluded from AI page sharing, which is off by default
Command palette (⌘K) for tabs and commands
caveats: Requires macOS 26.5 or later and Apple Silicon; it is Mac-only
Labeled a 0.1.3 development preview; only local MLX generation and Stop are described as verified, while cloud completions and wider browser compatibility need more testing
Building requires Xcode with the macOS 26.5 SDK and the Metal toolchain
